title: 27-year-old Calgarian dies in police custody
article: A Calgary family is left with grief and unanswered questions after a 27-year-old man died in police custody.

Tamer Sayed Roha died Wednesday night, shortly after police were called to the northwest Calgary hotel where he was staying -- a tragic end to what relatives say was a year-long struggle with substance abuse his mother tried in vain to stop.
And while Roha's mother said she will wait to find out what transpired Wednesday night, she said she's angry her efforts to compel her son to get treatment were stymied by the law.
"His mother has gone through every possible legal avenue she could explore," a relative said on behalf of Roha's mother Thursday night.

Roha's mother said she tried to force her son into treatment programs and even obtained a mental health warrant from the courts, but those actions didn't carry enough weight to hold and treat him against his will.
Someone in the grip of an addiction doesn't have a sound mind to make decisions about their well-being, Roha's mother said.
"We know you have to consider someone's individual rights, but what about the rights of the people who love that person and who want to get him help?" she said.
Roha's mother said her concerns are fuelled by what she describes as the uncaring attitude of five officers who arrested her son after he became violent at the family home Monday night.
Roha weighed approximately 120 pounds and his mother said she was concerned the officers would hurt him while making the arrest.
"There wasn't much compassion (from police) in that instance," the relative said.
Roha was a guest at the Quality Inn, 2359 Banff Tr. N.W., when police were called to his room around 10:25 p.m. after reports the man inside was acting oddly.

"He was yelling and screaming and disturbing other patrons of the hotel," said Staff Sgt. Bryant Petkau of the Calgary police homicide unit, which is called to investigate when anyone dies in police custody.
"At this point in time, we do not appear to have any criminal activity on behalf of members of the police service who were in attendance, or anyone in EMS," said Petkau.
"The police were trying to talk to him and calm him down, and at the same time, summoned EMS to come and give them a hand."
Police said Roha became violent and officers were forced to restrain him with handcuffs.
Shortly after paramedics arrived, Roha became passive and didn't appear to be breathing.
"He was transported to hospital by EMS and was pronounced dead at hospital," said Petkau.
Police said no drug paraphernalia was found in Roha's room and they are awaiting toxicology reports to determine the cause of death.
They would not speculate whether Roha died of a drug overdose, but said his "erratic" behaviour would be consistent with someone who had.
Roha's mother, who viewed his body Thursday, said her son's face was badly bruised and she wants any investigation to determine whether the actions of police contributed to his death.
"We don't want to point any fingers, but as his family, how can you not ask the question?" said the relative.
